findings.detail: A check that starts `sleep 600 >/dev/null 2>&1 &`, prints its expected marker and exits leaves that child running in the owned process group. Once both output pipes close, process.wait() reaps the leader and sets returncode, so this guard skips group cleanup. The step can satisfy its verdict while background processes survive restoration and final cleanup, leaking resources and potentially modifying files during subsequent phases.
findings.fix: Track and clean up owned process groups before reconstructing or discarding their subject tree, preserving process identity safely until cleanup. Add coverage for a child that redirects both streams and outlives its normally exiting parent.
findings.title: Uncited: Normally exiting steps can leave background descendants running.
